A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Robust-VLGuard and DiffPure-VLM work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, despite some incorrect cross-references in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-noise robustness evaluations, safety fine-tuning experiments, ablations, and adversarial-defense results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds baseline evaluation results in appendix Table 12.

M1.justification: The Robust-VLGuard construction, Gaussian-noise-augmented LoRA fine-tuning, and DiffPure-VLM purification procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the model-specific training components are retained.

E1.justification: Training-data sources and task coverage are unchanged, as are MM-Vet, RealToxicityPrompts, and the clean, Gaussian-noisy, and PGD-adversarial evaluation scenarios. The new appendix table uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 12 broadens the adversarial-purification comparison to include unmodified InternVL2 and LLaVA, and InternVL2-VLGuard and MiniGPT-4-VLGuard, where corresponding v1 comparisons lacked these configurations. Existing JailGuard comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Training settings, decoding procedures, evaluation metrics, noise levels, and attack and diffusion parameters are retained. Table 12 extends baseline reporting under the existing epsilon = 32/255 and t* = 50 protocol without introducing a different evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The instruction-ratio and training-epoch ablations, noise-level and diffusion-timestep sweeps, and pixel-space and embedding-space analyses are retained. The added table expands baseline comparisons without introducing a separate ablation or robustness scenario.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose three-run averaging for safety evaluation in Section 9.3 and retain the same uncertainty entries in Table 3. The added table continues point-estimate reporting without new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 corrects InternVL2-VLGuard's clean MM-Vet drop from -7.0 to -17.0 while retaining its 42.9 score. New Table 12 adds baseline ASR and toxicity results, including unmodified InternVL2's 65.0% under PGD and 53.1% after purification. v1 Table 12 is retained unchanged as v3 Table 13.

T1.justification: The kurtosis and Q-Q definitions, four Gaussian-noise conjectures, and Lipschitz and Taylor-expansion arguments in Sections 13–14 are retained. Mathematical changes are limited to punctuation and layout.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about Gaussian-noise vulnerability, Robust-VLGuard safety alignment, and DiffPure's distribution-shifting role. Introduction rewriting does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of noise sensitivity, safety–helpfulness tradeoffs, and diffusion timesteps remain unchanged. The existing limitation concerning resizing artifacts from the fixed-resolution diffusion model is also retained.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same model specifications, LoRA hyperparameters, batch size, hardware, training duration, diffusion checkpoint information, and code/data access statement. No additional implementation instructions accompany Table 12.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Fan et al.'s Unbridled Icarus survey and Szegedy's Intriguing Properties of Neural Networks in the introduction. The substantive positioning against existing defenses remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses several introduction paragraphs, edits grammar, and updates author information while retaining the section structure. Some revised appendix references become inconsistent, including references to Sections F and D.2 although the corresponding headings remain 13 and 11.2.

P2.justification: v3 adds appendix Table 12, retains the previous extended-results table as Table 13, compacts the author block, and relocates several figures and tables. Existing plots and diagrams retain their content and visual design.

improvement.justification: The added baseline results in appendix Table 12 make comparisons with unmodified and conventionally safety-tuned models more complete, while the Table 2 correction improves numerical accuracy. These provide a limited evidential improvement without changing the method or established findings. Newly inconsistent appendix references reduce navigability and temper the gain.
